I don't know much about the rendering process but it looks cool. How long did that take to render?
Thanks! This one took 6 hours but I might be able to reduce that time by tweaking some settings.

Wow, that is incredible - you're very patient :)

Probably a dumb question but why does it take so long? Is it zillions of calculations that get carried out?

It is easy to do it by letting it render while I sleep. The downside is I have woken up to find half way through the animation something goes wonky because I did some setting wrong. Even with that frustration I have enjoyed every minute of learning to use Blender for this stuff.

A lot of calculations that are all based on the path of light through the scene. It has to calculate how light refracts as it passes through the water, bounces of an object, and where it should terminate. Then it goes through a clean up process where some of the math involved in the lighting calculations comes out bad and leaves a pixel that is an off color just hanging around (usually referred to as fireflies).

I have to let it calculate the physics of the water separately, which takes about 30 minutes for the whole sequence. But the nice thing is that it caches that so I can go through the timeline without hiccups. So once I get the flow of things settled, I can spend a lot of time tinkering on a material or whatever and render a single frame to make sure it looks good.

I always thought of it as just a moving picture, I never considered all the complexities of how light reflects and bends. Thank you taking the time to explain that so well, it makes a lot of sense now. Keep up the great work :)
